title: Outside-In: Sell great support by demonstrating it, not announcing it
summary: Jason argues that claims like "unmatched customer service" are meaningless noise ("if it's on the outside, it's not on the inside"). Instead, invite prospects to test your support during the trial and let them draw their own conclusions. This builds trust during the initial demo.

principles.text: If something is true you don't need to announce it; loudly claiming a virtue signals it may be missing.
principles.quote: When something is true, you don't need to announce it. You don't need to convince people of it. You don't have to draw attention to it.

principles.text: You can't convince people you have good support by telling them; claiming it can even turn them off.
principles.quote: But you can't convince people you have good support by telling them so. In fact, telling them so might turn them off.

principles.text: In demos, invite prospects to trial your tech support alongside your software.
principles.quote: While you're trialing our software, also trial our tech support. Give 'em a call and test it out. Make sure we're responsive and helpful.

principles.text: Customers are numb to stock service slogans, so words alone are meaningless even when true.
principles.quote: People are so used to hearing things like "We have unbeatable customer service" and "Customer service is priority number one," the words are water off a duck's back. Even if true, they're meaningless.

principles.text: Great support drives relationships, word-of-mouth and can win a sale despite a weak first impression.
principles.quote: having good service is not only a competitive advantage, it's also the primary way to develop solid relationships, promote word-of-mouth advertising (the best kind), and can even make a sale even when the first impression was unfavorable.

principles.text: Don't say it, do it: encourage prospects to notice and let them reach their own conclusions.
principles.quote: So don't say it, do it. Encourage potential customers to notice, but let them come to their own conclusions.
